product_defects_surfaced_not_in_scope_to.description: main.py:18388-18399 calls create_capital_router(read_surface=app_deps.read_surface, ...) but never passes get_capital_authority. Inside CapitalService._authority() (capital/service.py:167-169), an absent get_capital_authority falls back to self._store() -- i.e. the same read-surface store backs both reads and the write/authority path for all 25 Capital routes. Writes are not provably dead (read_surface is a real, non-None ReadSurfacePorts instance, confirmed live at this head), but no code path currently supplies a dedicated capital-authority object, so any Capital write route the wiring intends to route to a distinct authority instead silently uses the read store.

The narrower, currently-reproducible gap is specifically that get_capital_authority is unwired, not that the read store is None. The successor triaging this should re-verify against current head rather than reuse the older 'resolved_get_read_store is None' description.
